words.gloss: abandonment of desire, anger, greed, pride, arrogance and joy

hindi: विद्या विनय का कारण; इन्द्रियों पर विजय काम, क्रोध, लोभ, अभिमान, मद, हर्ष के त्याग से करनी चाहिए।
english: Learning [is] the cause of discipline; conquest of the senses is to be accomplished through the abandonment of desire, anger, greed, pride, arrogance and joy.
notes: Verbless first clause: copula bracketed in English, none in Hindi. hetu = cause (could also be 'means'). jaya is rendered 'conquest' (glossary: control not used). māna = pride and mada = arrogance are the usual senses; harṣa = joy (exultation) kept literal. The six members form the traditional group of six enemies named in unit 11 (śatru-ṣaḍ-varga). kāryaḥ is a gerundive agreeing with indriya-jayaḥ.

words.gloss: of the ear, skin, eye, tongue and nose organs of sense
in sound, touch, form, taste and smell

hindi: कान, त्वचा, आँख, जीभ, नाक इन्द्रियों की शब्द, स्पर्श, रूप, रस, गन्ध में विचलन का अभाव इन्द्रिय-विजय; अथवा शास्त्र का अनुष्ठान।
english: Non-deviation of the ear, skin, eye, tongue and nose organs of sense in sound, touch, form, taste and smell [is] conquest of the senses, or the practice of the treatise.
notes: Verbless: copula bracketed in English only. avipratipatti (a-vi-prati-pad) is rendered literally 'non-deviation'; 'absence of wrong engagement' or 'non-contradiction' are possible. The first compound ends in indriya: 'the organs of sense (that are) ear, skin, eye, tongue, nose'. The vā is read as an alternative definition: 'or [conquest of the senses is] the practice of the treatise'; the second alternative could also be read as a separate predicate. anuṣṭhāna = carrying out, practice (Hindi अनुष्ठान kept, no ritual sense intended). The e-text spelling tvag is the sandhi form of tvac.

english: For this whole treatise [is] conquest of the senses.
notes: Verbless: copula bracketed in English only. hi rendered 'for' / क्योंकि. kṛtsnam is neuter, agreeing with śāstram. The sense is that the whole treatise has conquest of the senses as its content; the text does not say more.

words.gram: pron. n. (first member of a compound)

words.gloss: whose senses are not under control

hindi: उसके विरुद्ध आचरण वाला, वश में न रहने वाली इन्द्रियों वाला, चार अन्तों वाला भी राजा तुरन्त नष्ट हो जाता है।
english: A king whose conduct is contrary to that, whose senses are not under control, even one who is four-ended, perishes at once.

text_flags.why: possible stray space: tad is the first member of the compound tad-viruddha-vṛtti (the dot is expected after tad)

notes: The printed space after tad is flagged; read as a compound, 'whose conduct is contrary to that' (tat = the preceding teaching of the control of the senses). If tad were a separate word it would be 'therefore'. cāturanta is rendered literally 'four-ended'; it qualifies rājā (one whose rule reaches the four ends [of the earth] is the usual understanding, kept out of the text). avaśya-indriya = a-vaśya + indriya, 'whose senses are not controlled'.

words.gram: pres. part. ātm. m. nom. sg. abhi-√man

hindi: जैसे दाण्डक्य नामक भोज, काम से ब्राह्मण की कन्या को लक्ष्य बनाता हुआ, बन्धुओं और राष्ट्र सहित नष्ट हो गया, और वैदेह कराल।
english: As Dandakya by name, a Bhoja, aiming at a Brahmin's girl from desire, perished together with his relatives and kingdom, and Karala the Vaideha [perished].
notes: The verb vinanāśa is not repeated for Karāla, and the Hindi leaves it unrepeated. abhi-√man follows the glossary (7.16) 'aim at'; 'covet' or 'lay claim to' are the usual senses and are left to the reader. bhoja: kept as a name; it may be a clan/people name ('a Bhoja'). vaideha = of Videha, kept as 'the Vaideha'. sa-bandhu-rāṣṭra is a bahuvrīhi 'with relatives and kingdom'; the sa is a prefix joined by '-' in the e-text and is given its own entry. The yathā has no tathā in the unit: the sentence continues in the following units as a list of examples (no GROUPING problem).

hindi: क्रोध से ब्राह्मणों पर आक्रमण करने वाला जनमेजय, और भृगुओं पर तालजङ्घ
english: From anger Janamejaya, having attacked the Brahmins, and Talajangha [having attacked] the Bhrigus.
notes: Elliptical list: the finite verb (perished, vinanāśa of unit 5) is understood, not stated, and is not supplied in either language. vikrānta (vi-√kram) = having advanced (hostilely), rendered 'attacked' in line with vikrama = attack (7.8). The locatives brāhmaṇeṣu, bhṛguṣu are read as 'against'.

words.gram: pres. part. ātm. caus. m. nom. sg. ati-ā-√hṛ

hindi: लोभ से चारों वर्णों से अत्यधिक मँगवाने वाला ऐल, और सौवीर अजबिन्दु
english: From greed Aila, making the four varṇas bring in excess, and Ajabindu the Sauvira.
notes: Elliptical list as in unit 6: no finite verb is stated. atyāhārayamāṇaḥ (ati-ā-√hṛ, causative) is obscure: literally 'causing to bring in excess'; 'exacting excessively from the four varṇas' is the probable sense and is kept in notes only. cāturvarṇya = the fourfold varṇa order, 'the four varṇas'. Sauvīra = of the Sauvīra people, kept as 'the Sauvira'. The '-' in ca-ajabinduḥ is the e-text's unsandhied join of two words.

words.gram: pres. part. m. nom. sg. a-pra-√yam

hindi: मान से दूसरों की स्त्रियों को न देने वाला रावण, और दुर्योधन राज्य से अंश
english: From pride Ravana, not giving up others' wives, and Duryodhana [not giving] a share from the kingdom.
notes: Elliptical: the participle aprayacchan is not repeated for Duryodhana, nor is any finite verb stated; the English brackets the repeated participle, the Hindi leaves it out. dāra is a plural masculine noun (wives); para = others' (glossary 9.2: pare = the others). pra-√yam 'give, hand over', rendered 'not giving up'. The ca stands after aṃśam and links the second example to the first; it is rendered 'and' before Duryodhana.

hindi: मद से प्राणियों का अपमान करने वाला दम्भोद्भव, और हैहय अर्जुन
english: From arrogance Dambhodbhava, despiser of beings, and Arjuna the Haihaya.
notes: Elliptical list, no finite verb stated (see unit 6). dambhodbhava is kept as a name (literally 'arisen from deceit'); it may be a title or epithet. bhūta = beings (creatures); avamānin = one who despises. Haihaya = of the Haihaya people; this Arjuna is not the Pandava.

words.gram: pres. part. caus. m. nom. sg. ati-ā-√sad

hindi: हर्ष से अगस्त्य पर आक्रमण करने वाला वातापि, और वृष्णि-संघ द्वैपायन को
english: From joy Vatapi, assailing Agastya, and the Vrishni saṅgha [assailing] Dvaipayana.
notes: Elliptical list, no finite verb stated. atyāsādayan (ati-ā-√sad, causative) 'causing to approach too far, assailing'; the sense is uncertain ('offending', 'harassing' are possible). saṅgha is kept (saṅgha, glossary 11.1), no 'republic'. The closing iti has no opening quotation and is not rendered; it closes the series of examples begun at 'yathā' in unit 5.

hindi: ये और दूसरे, बहुत से राजा, शत्रुओं के छह-वर्ग का आश्रय लिए हुए, बन्धुओं और राष्ट्रों सहित नष्ट हो गए, अजित इन्द्रियों वाले।
english: Both these and others, many kings, having resorted to the sixfold group of enemies, perished together with their relatives and kingdoms, their senses unconquered.
notes: ete ca anye ca bahavaḥ: 'both these and other, many' (ca ... ca, glossary 7.5). The sixfold group of enemies (śatru-ṣaḍ-varga) is the six named in unit 1 (desire, anger, greed, pride, arrogance, joy); the text of this unit does not list them. The sa of sa-bandhu-rāṣṭrāḥ is a prefix of a bahuvrīhi; the e-text joins it with '-'.

hindi: शत्रुओं के छह-वर्ग को त्यागकर जित इन्द्रियों वाले जामदग्न्य और नाभाग अम्बरीष दोनों ने चिर काल तक पृथ्वी का भोग किया।
english: Jamadagnya, having abandoned the sixfold group of enemies, with his senses conquered, and Ambarisha Nabhaga both enjoyed the earth for long.
notes: bubhujāte is dual, hence 'both' / दोनों; the two subjects are Jāmadagnya and Ambarīṣa Nābhāga. Jāmadagnya (descendant of Jamadagni) and Nābhāga (descendant of Nabhaga) are patronymics kept as names; no further identification is made. √bhuj 'enjoy' is kept literal (enjoy / possess).
